newsitem.title: MEXICO: KN Energy wins Mexico natgas concession.
newsitem.headline: KN Energy wins Mexico natgas concession.

text.p: KN Energy was declared the winner of the rights to distribute natural gas in the region surrounding Hermosillo, Sonora state, Mexico's Energy Regulatory Commission (CRE) said in a public ceremony on Wednesday.

KN Energy won the concession after Argentine competitor Compania General de Combustibles, a private company, did not pass the technical requirements set down in the bidding process, said CRE president Hector Olea.

The Denver, Colorado-based company offered to charge consumers $3.59 per gigacalorie, and pledging to service aminimum client base of 26,250 residential customers in the first five years of its concession.

With the winning bid, KN Energy possesses exclusive rights in the region for 12 years and distribution rights for 30 years to the more than 600,000 people that live in Hermosillo and surrounding cities of Guaymas and Empalme.

The Sonora state site in the third in a series of natural gas distribution sites auctioned to private bidders in a move to boost infrastructure and use of the fuel, which will continue to be provided by state oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex).
The first two sites, Mexicali and Chihuahua, were won by a U.S.-Mexican consortium composed of U.S. firms Pacific Enterprises and Enova International with Mexican Proxima.
